name: Kadung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Decker et al. 2021 SIL sociolinguistic survey found; no phonology/grammar located

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2022. The Vaghat language of Central Nigeria (Introduction to Vaghat language). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, 17 pp.
sources.note: Sister variety (Vaghat = Bijim/Legeri per Blench's abstract, glottocode of Bijim not Kadung); likely contains a Tones section in Blench's standard format; would give the cluster-level prosodic picture.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021. The Kwaŋ language of Central Nigeria and its affinities (2021 version, printout June 13, 2021), 27 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Academia.edu 49231501
sources.note: Body text embedded in the Internet Archive copy of the academia.edu page (PDF itself needs a login). Sec. 3.3 Tones reads in full: 'Kwaŋ appears to have three level tones and rising and falling tones.' Also: plural marked by tone change Low/High or Mid/High in a few nouns. No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the whole embedded text.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kwanka language' (wikitext), listing Blench 2021 Kwaŋ, Blench 2022 Vaghat, Blench 2022 Vaghat religion, Blench 2023 Sur-Myet
sources.note: Used only for discovery of the Blench 2021/2022 KWEF papers and their academia.edu URLs.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page vagh1248 'Kadung' and reference records 161236 (Blench 2007) and 590888 (Decker et al. 2021)
sources.note: No descriptive (grammar/phonology) reference listed; only overview/wordlist items.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Luther Hon, Julius Dabet, Benard Abraham & Innocent Jonah. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Bijim [jbm] Language of Plateau and Bauchi States, Nigeria, with Mention of the Kadung [dkg] and Tiyaa [tyy] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-033, 72 pp. SIL International.
sources.note: Sec. 6.3 'Phonetic inventory of Bijim-Kadung-Tiyaa' gives consonant/vowel tables only ('initial, cursory observations'); Appendix E states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Nothing on stress. Two Kadung wordlists (Mwel, Kwanka villages) with tone diacritics. downloaded via the Internet Archive (SIL's PDF path is could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-035 (split [bij] into Bijim [jbm], Kadung [dkg], Tiyaa [tyy]) with New Code Request forms, submitted by Christina Riepe, SIL Nigeria.
sources.note: Names, villages, lexicostatistical percentages only; no phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007. The Kwaŋ language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 5 September 2007, 28 pp. Cambridge: ms. (Glottolog ref 161236, listed by Glottolog as a wordlist)
sources.note: Section 3 'Phonology' (vowels, consonants) is explicitly 'tentative'; section 3.3 'Tones' is an empty heading (no text) in this draft; wordlist is tone-marked; no mention of stress or accent anywhere. downloaded from the the Internet Archive (2024-11-17 capture of rogerblench.info; the live site could not be reached by automated download/bot-challenge by automated download).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. Tarok and related languages of east-central Nigeria: nomenclature and subclassification. Draft, printout 22 October 2004, 21 pp.
sources.note: Kwanka appears only in scattered cognate comparisons; no phonology of Kwanka, no stress statement (tone remarks concern Tarok only).

sources.citation: Norton, Russell. 2019a. Bijim Linguistic Consultant Report. ms. SIL Nigeria; Norton, Russell. 2019b. A First Bijim-English Dictionary. ms. SIL Nigeria.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only linguist's analysis of the closely related Bijim [jbm] (cited by Blench 2021 for number marking by tone and consonant mutation); a consultant report would normally state tone (and any stress) facts; unpublished SIL manuscripts.
